paras: The killing of Dave Ball was the shooting of a Black man near Senatobia, Tate County, Mississippi, in August 1880 by W. R. McNorton, who had been keeping watch for him at a house. Ball was accused of trying to enter the rooms of women in the house, and a coroner's jury ruled the killing justifiable homicide. A Jackson weekly printed the story as "Got What He Deserved."

According to the Memphis Avalanche, Ball, "a colored man," had repeatedly tried to enter ladies' rooms in a house on Capt. Shandy's plantation, two miles from Senatobia. Another brief said he had tried for several nights to enter the sleeping room of McNorton's daughter.

McNorton and a friend, both armed, waited for Ball, and early on a Monday morning he came to the window of a room occupied by two young ladies. Ordered to halt, he ran, and a load of buckshot struck him in the back; he died within minutes. The brief gave the time as 2 o'clock on a Tuesday morning and said McNorton shot Ball in the head, killing him instantly.

McNorton went at once to a magistrate and reported what he had done. The inquest jury, as published by the Senatobia Express, found that Ball was killed while forcing entry into W. G. Wilson's house, where McNorton boarded, with intent to rape, and that the homicide was "under the law and under the facts, justifiable." No report of an arrest or further proceedings appears in the coverage.

The Jackson Weekly Clarion of August 18 printed the Avalanche account and the Express verdict under the headline "Got What He Deserved," calling Ball "the scoundrel." On August 22 the Dallas Daily Herald ran the brief among Mississippi crop and weather items, calling Ball "a scoundrelly negro" and "the villain." Both versions rest on the shooters' side and the inquest; no Black-press coverage was found.
The versions differ on the day (Monday or Tuesday), the wound (back or head), whose room was at issue (two young ladies' or McNorton's daughter's), and whether a friend was present.

reader.title: Killing of Dave Ball
bases: Ball was shot by one or two armed private men keeping watch at a house, not by a mob, band or posse, and an inquest ruled it justifiable homicide (A3, A4).

The Memphis Avalanche account with the Senatobia Express inquest verdict (A3) and a separately worded Mississippi brief (A4) agree that McNorton shot Dave Ball near Senatobia and that the killing was ruled justifiable, though both rest on the shooters' side.

accounts.label: Memphis Avalanche
accounts.gist: Ball, after several attempts to enter ladies' rooms, approached the window of two young ladies early Monday; ordered to halt by the watching McNorton and a friend, he ran and was shot in the back with buckshot, dying in a few minutes.

accounts.label: Coroner's jury (via Senatobia Express)
accounts.gist: Ball was killed while attempting to force entry into W. G. Wilson's house, where McNorton boarded, intending rape; the homicide was justifiable.

accounts.label: Mississippi brief
accounts.gist: After several nights of attempts on the sleeping room of McNorton's daughter, Ball was shot in the head at 2 a.m. Tuesday by McNorton, who reported to a magistrate; an inquest found the killing justifiable.

framing.detail: The Jackson Weekly Clarion headlined the item 'Got What He Deserved' and called Ball 'the scoundrel'.
The Dallas Daily Herald's Mississippi column called Ball 'a scoundrelly negro' and 'the villain' and gave only the shooter's side.

conflicts.note: Neither account gives a calendar date; the Clarion version (A3) is the earlier print.
